properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/20/2025 to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/20/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8238473
Permit API: 081-21995
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/20/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of about 20 gallons of produced fluid. The release occurred while a water truck was removing fluid from the temporary storage tanks onsite.Tobias arrived onsite to screen and remediate the impacted area. A vac truck was used to remove some fluid and surface material. The rest of the remediation involved scraping an area that was approximately 100' long by 63' wide. The excavation averaged 1-2" deep with occasional depths of about 8". There was about 40 tons of material removed and placed into 2 dumpsters for disposal.There were some puddles on the pad surface that were screened for conductivity. Those readings ranged between 0.49 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) and 1.07 mS/cm. Soil conductivity immediately off the pad and behind the release ranged between 0.15 - 0.18 mS/cm while a puddle in that area was 0.45 mS/cm (Photos 4 and 5). Continuing downslope, conductivities of puddles in the compost filter sock (CFS) were 0.87 - 1.01 mS/cm. The readings continued to drop as the downslope infiltration berms were screened. The conductivity in front of the berm was 0.37 mS/cm and behind the berm it was 0.1 mS/cm. Moving east along the pad and uphill from the release soil conductivities ranged between 0.70 and 0.83 mS/cm and conductivities of puddles were between 1.03 and 1.09 mS/cm.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted and Immediately Corrected for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). It is recommended that the pad be screened under the secondary containment when it is eventually removed.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PETRO ERIE INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/31/2023
Violation Code: OGA3217(A) - PROTECTION OF FRESH GROUNDWATER AND CASING REQUIREMENTS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to control and dispose of brines produced from the drilling, alteration or operation of a well consistent with the Clean Streams Law.
Violation ID: 8154300
Permit API: 121-45433
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/31/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. An onsite meeting was scheduled with Petro Erie Inc. and the Department which developed this Inspection Report.Individuals present at the onsite meeting:Harry Rhoades -Owner/Operator of Petro Erie Inc.Chris Rhoades -Driver for Harry RhoadesRob Bechtel -PA DEPRick Willey -PA DEPAlan Wolf -PA DEPLucas Eichner -PA DEPSteve Wells -PA DEPThe meeting was started off by Rob Bechtel stating the reason for the meeting and what was discovered during a previous site inspection on 7/21/2023 with violations cited. It was discussed that there is a potential that the discharge of produced fluid from the tank battery may have impacted the Reno, PA public water supply. Mr. Rhoades asked if the pubic water supply was now safe to drink and if regular testing was being conducted. We informed him that the oil and gas program was collecting samples for analysis to determine if the water supply was impacted by oil and gas activity and that the Safe Drinking Water program was working with Venango Water Company related to the public water supply. The discussion with Mr. Rhoades made him aware of the fact that there are more than several concerns with his lease. The Department recommended that he hire an environmental consultant to help him through the cleanup and reporting process of an Act 2 cleanup regarding the discharge of produced fluid and the potential impact of the Reno public water supply. Other violations were discussed regarding the other wells on his lease. Statements that were made by Mr. Rhoades during the meeting:-He is the only owner/operator of Petro Erie Inc-He pumps the wells on the lease himself-One well on the lease is on a timer and pumps when he is not present-Mr. Rhoades does not know what occurred at the site referring to the discharge of produced fluid-Wants the water of the households in Reno tested-Hauled 3 loads of brine, 1 load hauled by Gavin to disposal in OH and 2 loads hauled by Paul Weaver to a frac job in West Virginia-Stated that the tank battery and the impact area was present when he purchased the lease

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78a and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected.
Violation ID: 8160130
Permit API: 015-23768
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/21/2023
Comments: I arrived to the location at 12:50pm. The weather was 68¿¿F and sunny at time of inspection. I met with Repsol representative Billy Watts on location for the inspection. Plugging work was being performed on this well (9H) at time of inspection. A gel plug was set in the hole with a top at 2,630'. The rig was planning to next run a Cement Bond Log (CBL) and continue with plugging operations. On 9/21/2023 (prior to my arrival onsite), the production casing was section milled and approximately 13’ of damaged casing was removed from the well. I visually inspected the section of removed casing during this inspection. The piece of casing that was on top of the 5 1/2" production casing string was a 3' pup joint. Approximately 1 1/2' down the 3' pup joint, 3 holes were noted in the casing. The dimensions of the holes ranged in size from approximately 1/8" to 2" and varied from a straight-lined crack to irregular and rounded in shape. While the damaged casing was visually observed during the inspection, Repsol did restrict my ability to document the condition of the removed section of casing by photograph. Although, Repsol provided photographs of the removed section of casing to the Department the next day (9/22/2023), this represents a violation of Section 3258(a) of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. ¿¿ 3258(a). I left the location at 1:45pm. In addition to citing this new violation, the outstanding violations that were previously cited (Inspection Record #3611541) were also noted as continuing during this inspection. Therefore, the Inspection Results Code used for this inspection report is Violation(s) and Recurring Violations (VRV). The PADEP requests that Respol include an explanation of the cause of this violation with the written response previously-requested in the NOV dated 8/28/2023 (Inspection Record #3611541).

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PETRO ERIE INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/21/2023
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8153361
Permit API: 121-45433
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/21/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023.There is an active discharge of fluid from the Tank Battery of the Lower Reno oil lease that is permitted and operated by Petro Erie Inc.. The public water supply for the town of Reno, PA is under a "Do Not Consume Advisory" based upon an increase in TDS for the Bellows Spring Cistern (owned and operated by Venango Water Company).The tank battery consists of (2) 210bbl steel tanks and (4) 100bbl poly tanks. The earthen dike appears to be lined with a plastic liner. There is a dike drain that is located in the southwest corner of the dike. The valve on the drain pipe is open and fluid is flowing to the ground. The area inside the dike appears to have been impacted by produced fluid from the tanks. A pipeline between two of the poly tanks was actively dripping fluid. Field screening inside the dike were conducted with the soil probe for conductivity, and all readings were above the range of the meter (20,000uS).The discharge from the dike drain flows south across an open area and into a wooded area. There is a visible impact area extending from the dike drain in an irregular pattern approximately 80 yards from the earthen dike and approximately ranging from 6' to 25' in width. Field screening within the impacted area was conducted approximately every 10 yards. Conductivity measurements ranged from 11,000uS to above the range of the meter (20,000uS). Several areas outside of the impacted area were checked with the soil probe and the levels ranged between 60uS to 164uS. An oil sheen is visible within the flowing water and dead vegetation is also observed including several large cherry trees within the impacted area. The amount of discharged fluid is unknown and based upon the observations onsite it appears that the discharge has been occurring for some time.The dike drain was closed by DEP staff at 8:45am to stop the continued discharge of fluid outside of the earthen dike.Water samples were collected at the dike drain outlet (discharge point) and sent to the lab for analysis. Water samples were also collected at the Bellows Spring Cistern (41.422360 -79.764490) which is a source for a public water supply of the town of Reno, PA.While onsite the Department talked with the operator/owner (Harry Rhoades) via a phone conversation. The discharge and the potential that the discharge may be impacting the public water supply was discussed with Mr. Rhoades. Mr. Rhoades insisted that he does not discharge his brine and that he could provide disposal documents. It was stated that the dike drain was left open because of forecasted rain. Violations are cited.The Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI) will be conducting a separate well compliance inspection for the well and other wells on the lease.

Violation ID: 911087

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/18/2021
Comments: On 03/18/2021, Department of Environmental Protection representative John Ciccone (Water Quality Specialist) conducted an inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s (CALLC) MAGGIE location in response to a spill notification (Complaint ID # 355355). Eric Hottenstein (CALLC HSE Supervisor) reported the release at 0700 hours on 03/18/2021. Mr. Hottenstein’s initial report stated that he was notified that an estimated 100 gallons of Blue Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF), an additive for diesel fuel, was spilled onto the western side of the pad surface. According to the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) on DEF, the substance is a mixture of 67.5% water and 32.5% urea by weight (photo # 9). The spill occurred when a 400-gallon tote of DEF was punctured by a forklift while repositioning the tote onto containment. Fluid that was pooled on the pad surface was vacuumed up and impacted soils were excavated. Excavated soils were placed within containment. I arrived onsite at 1051 hours. The weather was 43 degrees with steady rainfall. CALLC crews were present onsite and preparing for stimulation operations, scheduled to begin today (03/18/2021). I checked in with Brent Thomas (CALLC Safety Manager) to announce my presence and in order to be guided to the release location. I observed 2 separate containments, each approximately 12 feet x 12 feet in dimension, that excavated soils were staged within (photo # 1, 2). Excavated soils were covered with tarp, and containments had berms present. A vacuum truck was parked at the location of release at the time of my arrival (photo # 3). Mr. Thomas instructed to truck to move so I could gather observations. According to photographs of the initial release, an area of approximately 20 feet x 20 feet was impacted (photo # 15). Comments: This inspection is in response to a complaint of a spill on 03/07/2022 located at the Armac lease on Bauer Hill road. The complainant reported a strong smell and saw diapers and oil booms in the Bauer Hill road ditch as well as inside the containment diking. Upon responding to the complaint, and speaking with Vince Bailey the pumper for the lease he reported that the storage tank had over flowed on Saturday March 5th, he cleaned up the oil inside containment he estimated the spill at 2.5 barrels. Monday crude oil had breached the diking by migrating through the pervious material used in the construction of the containment. The crude oil flowed down slope approx 250 feet into a road side ditch on Bauer Hill road, it continued another 275 feet into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Glade Run. There was evidence of crude along the tributary to its confluence of Glad Run. An unknown amount of crude oil was released and made its way into waters of the Commonwealth.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 995302
Permit API: 015-21185
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/08/2023
Comments: On 5/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection at the Repsol Alderson V 05-009 well site. This was in response to a spill notification of five gallons of antifreeze that the department received from Repsol on 5/6/2023.Prior to arrival at the site, I contacted JD Ressler of Repsol, the person who had submitted the notification of the spill to the department. JD said that at approximately 2:30 AM on 5/6/2023, a truck driver drove over a concrete barricade, dragging the barricade along under his truck for a distance on the pad surface. The concrete barricade did damage an antifreeze line on the truck, releasing approximately 5 gallons of antifreeze to the pad surface. Upon discovery, the leak was stopped and oil soaks were placed on the pad surface to absorb the fluid. The contaminated oil soaks were placed into trash bags. This waste material was brought to the Warner 05121 well site in Susquehanna county where fracking operations are currently being conducted. The waste material will be disposed by Environmental Resources out of Tunkhannock, PA.It was 55 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. Repsol is using the Alderson V 009 location to stage trucks that are servicing a nearby frac site in Susquehanna County. Sand and water trucks were on location, driving in and out during the inspection. At the site, I met with Repsol's Andrew Senefelder. Andrew led me to the location of the spill. Andrew said that the truck driver did run over and drag one concrete block, and also drug another concrete block that was attached via a cable. These concrete blocks are approximately 2' x 2' x 8' and can be viewed in pictures 3 and 4. I did look around the area described as where the spill took place. I screened water puddles in the area for conductivity with results at 0.4 mS conductance or less. I also viewed the puddles and the surface of the ground. I did not witness any discoloration or evidence of contamination in this area. Discussing the location of the waste, Andrew did say that the contaminated material was being brought back to this well site and would be disposed of from this site.Water puddles from recent rainfall were scattered across the pad surface. I field tested these for conductivity with results at 0.4 mS or less. I did not witness the emergency response plan at the entrance to the facility. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by two bio retention basins. Bio retention basin 1 is adequately stabilized and functioning as designed with minimal evidence of standing water. Bio retention basin 2 does have wetland foliage and standing water.There was one well staged for production. The well was tagged with the API/well permit number. No bubbling within the cellar was observed. The GPU and production tank had secondary containment. This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; SWMA 301, CSL 402, and 25 PA Code 78a.56. The spill had been cleaned up, resulting in VIOICs (Violation noted and Immediately Corrected).The DEP recommends the following: 1. Screen the area impacted by the release of antifreeze for additional contamination and continue with cleanup as necessary.2. Assess the stability and functionality of bio retention basin 2 and repair as necessary.3. Place a copy of the site emergency response plan at the entrance to the facility.I left the site at 1330 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/21/2026 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Township, Tioga county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/21/2026
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8271505
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/21/2026
Comments: On 4/21/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 52 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Adam Pierce who described current operations as follows: Evolution Well Services has been on site since 2/13/2026, performing stimulation operations on eight recently drilled gas wells. The crew was currently alternating between the 70HU, 204HU, 203HU, and 72HU. The crew has completed conducting stimulation stages on the other four wells. Adam expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by 6/8/2026.In addition to 28 frac tanks that were stationed on the west side of the pad during previous operations, four freshwater frac tanks, four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks have been staged on the pad. These tanks are staged in secondary containment.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs that are connected to the completed wells are stationed in secondary containment.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. During the inspection, I screened liquid in a 3' x 1.5' x 5" deep puddle, above the center outfall on the north side of the pad, the result being 9.40 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-242 from the puddle.I screened liquid flowing into the southeast corner of the sediment basin from the rock lined outfall from the pad, the result being 10.30 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-243 from the flowing liquid.I screened liquid in the sediment pond next to the east overflow, the result being 3.04 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-244 from the pond.I screened liquid flowing north from the sediment basin, past the last compost filter sock and past the LOD, the result being 3.33 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-245 from the flowing liquid.The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade with vegetation becoming effective. Separate construction projects are underway, installing water and gas pipelines on the south side of the pad.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1545 hours.

Comments: On 10/12/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 09/26/2023 (IR 3620008, Enforcement 419234).On 09/26/2023, violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, and SWMA 301 for the releases of production fluid were issued as outstanding. Violations of 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a) were issued for the accelerated erosion and lack of maintenance of the access road. The following was observed during inspection on 10/12/2023:While onsite, I called Paul Stiner of Diversified to discuss the observations regarding the production fluid within the berm and behind tank 5.A relatively small area behind tank 5 yielded some higher readings, but not as high as noted in inspection 3620008 (Photos 1-3). It is recommended to scrape up this area to ensure there are no residual areas of fluid. Between inspections, rain most likely diluted anything remaining.The valve on tank 4 appeared to have been replaced. The ground under the original valve appeared to have been remediated as seen by adequate readings and buckets onsite (Photos 4-7).Adjacent to the valve on tank 4, the lower section of the berm displayed elevated readings (Photos 8-11).The berm overall in this area appeared to require remediation to ensure no areas of elevated conductivity remain both inside and outside of the berm (Photos 12, 13).The access road appeared to remain in poor condition (Photos 14, 15).Due to the observations regarding the elevated conductivity readings and the condition of the access road, violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a) remain outstanding.

Comments: Incident Inspection of Expand's "Dunham" Marcellus well site.Expand is using this Marcellus well pad to stage equipment for hydraulically fracturing Marcellus wells at their nearby "Henry" site. Steve Moyer (Expand) called the DEP on Saturday January 18, 2025 to report an estimated 45-50 gallon release of produced liquid from an unknown source to the pad surface they discovered that day at 1445 hrs. Creston Environmental delineated the impacted area of the pad surface at approximately 35'x35' using electrical conductivity (EC) meters. They excavated to remove impacted pad material the day after its discovery. Creston sampled the pad material in accordance to Act 2 cleanup.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site, but cannot fully assess stabilization because of partial snow cover. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation on site. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Both Marcellus well cellars are full of snow/ice.I did not see any pooled water on the pad surface, just snow/ice. I could not get electrical conductivity readings with a Hanna Soil Test probe because the pad material is frozen solid. Air temp 27FJLP

Comments: I received a text message on April 3rd 2023 from the OGI that was checking on the flaring operation being conducted on the Hill Lease in Brokenstraw twp Warren county operated by Universal Resource Holdings. He said there was a oil spill that appears to have taken place awhile ago coming from a well close to the one being flared. On 04/04/2023, I followed up on the information, Brad Hofert from Universal resource holding was onsite at the time of my inspection. Brad said a valve had frozen and blew out on the number 21 well over winter. The valve was replaced and absorbent pads were used to clean up around the wellhead. I returned to the site on 04/05/2023 to gather photos and take another look at the extent of the spill.Evidence of the crude made it down slope approx 150 feet but stayed inside the tire ruts. More than likely carried by snow melt and rain. Oil soaked leaves and some oxidized crude can be seen in the tire ruts. The estimated release amount is around 5 gallons of crude. I spoke with Brad about getting the oil soaked leaf litter cleaned up and some of the soil next to the well head removed. He agreed and said he would get a crew together and a mini excavator to scrape up the area near the well head. With the estimated volume of this release and the small affected area, this is a non reportable release. The oil covered leaf litter and impacted soil will need to be properly disposed of.

Violation Code: 78.64(d)2 - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator drained tank containment facilities without responsible supervision and failed to follow proper drainage procedure.
Violation ID: 964817
Permit API: 083-57144
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Keating Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/09/2022
Comments: This conventional well has recently been produced with a pump jack, there was no activity on this location or throughout the Cole Creek lease during this inspection.A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl steel stock tank and a poly brine/production water tank is located approximately 150 feet to the south of this well. These tanks are contained by an earthen dyking which has been lined and partially filled with gravel. Holes have formed throughout the exposed portion of the liner along the upper edge of the containment wall.Fluid was trickling out of the containment drain pipe into the roadside ditch upon my arrival at the tank battery. There was no supervision of this discharge and the drain is not equipped with a valve. A shower drain cover was fitted onto the inlet of this drain. The specific conductivity (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment exceeded the upper threshold of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Pooled fluid in the ditch was also greater than 20,000 uS/cm. Deer tracks are abundant around the pooled fluid in the roadside ditch. This evidence suggests that the fluid being discharged from the containment drain is production water/brine. An SAC 941 sample was collected from the fluid discharging from the drain. The fluid in the roadside ditch flowed through a cross culvert and into a forested area. Poor road conditions have allowed stormwater to run off of the road surface above this culvert, which allowed the released fluid to migrate further into the forested area. Elevated SPC of pooled water and soil (along with stressed vegetation) was observed in various pathways across the forest floor west of the tank battery for approximately 200 feet downslope of the tank battery. The most downward extent of the apparent impacted soil (near a property boundary/corner marker) is approaching a channel (currently dry) that develops into an unnamed tributary of Cole Creek.After this inspection, I spoke with Justin Hansen of Bull Run to discuss the aforementioned issues along with concerns regarding the roads, site identification and actions necessary to consider this well site restored. In order to consider utilizing the containment drain, the fluid that is currently pooled inside of the containment will need to be removed along with the saturated gravel. Prior to any future discharges from the drain, the water should be tested as per the regulations to ensure it meets the criteria to be released under sufficient supervision.Future inspections will be conducted to review the current state of affairs with Bull Run personnel and evaluate remediation measures outside of the containment as they take place.

Comments: On September 18 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Kepple 4H Well.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared to be stabilized. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. It appears a site ID sign (Act 9 sign) was previously present at the access road entrance, however at the time of the inspection, only the stakes/posts remain.The Department recommends the operator ensure an Act 9 sign is installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency plan (PPC) were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of inspection, the well site appeared overgrown with vegetation. The well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present on the well head at the time of this inspection, and a well posting was present on the GPU. The Department recommends updating the well posting to ensure all information in legible. There were no observed leaks or discharge of fluid on the ground or around the wellhead. One production tank was present onsite, however appeared to be unconnected and not in use. There also appeared to be a a another GPU behind the 5H GPU and the Department was unable to discern if it was in use. A barrel of methanol was also observed onsite and did not appear to be with in secondary containment. The Department recommends ensuring all regulated substances are placed with in proper secondary containment, and remove any equipment not necessary for production from the site. There were no visible leaks of fluid with the GPU and it appeared not to be in secondary containment, however the well was drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The GPU did appear to have signs of corrosion, therefore the Department recommends the operator assess the structural integrity all production equipment on site.While onsite, the Department spoke to operator representative Heather Empfield via phone call and discussed the Department's findings. Ms.Empfield stated she would get an Act 9 sign ordered and installed at the site as well as ensure field staff assess the site and correct any issues as needed.Based on todays inspection, violations are being issued for the Act 9 sign, observed corrosion on the GPU, production equipment on site not in use, and the regulated substance(s) not in secondary containment.

Violation ID: 8174743
Permit API: 027-21517
Unconventional: Yes
County: Centre
Municipality: Burnside Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/08/2024
Comments: Rick Hall of EQT reported a spill to the Department on 2/6/24. Mr. Hall reported that during the plugging operation of well 027-21517 on 1/23/24, they were flowing the well to a gas buster and a spray/mist came out of the gas buster. It was estimated as 3 gallons at the time so it wasnt reported to DEP at that time. They scraped it up.On 2/5/24, they discovered that since 1/23/24, things have warmed up, there has been melting, and they discovered water that had elevated conductivity. They scraped some additional material and found that the spill is deeper than originally expected. I conducted an incident inspection on 2/8/24 with Bo Hampson of EQT. According to Mr. Hampson, all impacted materials have been scraped up and removed from the site. Evaluated readings were found under the gas buster so for now, the operator has installed additional containment on both sides of the gas buster. Once the plugging operation is ceased, they will remove the gas buster, containment, and further investigate the impacted area. I conducted field screenings on various spots near the gas buster and throughout the well pad using a Hanna Gro Line Soil probe. Readings ranged from 0.01 mS/cm to 0.62 mS/cm near the gas buster. I was unable to screen right next to the gas buster due to additional containment. Please contact notify me when the gas buster will be removed from the site so I can conduct additional screenings. The Department recommends that the operator pursue Act 2 due to the unknown volume. Violations have been cited.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. This is the 6th post CET deployment PBUTs being performed on the 21HC, 22HC and the 23HC and the 1st PBUTs performed on the 5H and 6H since Perf. and Squeeze ops were completed on 5/16/22. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. Comments: This well was inspected as part of a water supply complaint investigation involving a private water supply (CTS#379698). ¿¿ This well is located approximately 700’ east of the complainants water well. ¿¿ The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, corrosion, and possible failures. ¿¿ All valves were open, and the well is currently equipped for production.¿¿ ¿¿ No check valve was in place on the production line. ¿¿ The Well Records were reviewed to assist in the investigation.¿¿¿¿ ¿¿ Production and Mechanical Integrity Assessment Reports were reviewed and are not current.¿¿ The last reports submitted for mechanical integrity assessment was reporting year 2019. The last report submitted for production was reporting year 2020. ¿¿ As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. ¿¿ NO methane was detected in the slam bar holes utilizing a BASCOM-TURNER GAS EXPLORER II meter which was calibrated on 0405/2024. ¿¿ At this time the Department is issuing the following violations for the lack of production reporting, lack of mechanical integrity assessment reporting, lack of check valves on a production line, and failure to plug a well upon abandoning it. ¿¿ 78.121(A) – WELL REPORTING – PRODUCTION REPORTING – Conventional operator failed to submit annual conventional production and status report for permitted or registered well. ¿¿ 78.88(A)_ - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to record inspection results and retain records for at least 5 years for review by the Department. ¿¿ 78.88(b)1-4 – OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS – Operator failed to meet minimum requirements for inspections to determine compliance with the well construction and operating requirements. ¿¿ 78.73(f) – GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION – Operator failed to equip well with a check valve to prevent backflow from the pipelines into the well. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-11-24 to Range Resources Appalachia Llc in Amwell Twp, Washington county. properties.content:
Report Details

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 869682
Permit API: 125-28720
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Amwell Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-11-24
Comments: On November 24, 2019, I conducted an inspection of the Kingston 11485 Well 5H well in Amwell Twp., Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of Oil Base Drill Mod (OBM) reported 11/23/2019 at 09:10pm. The Operator reported that approximately 3 barrels of OBM was discovered around the cellar in the process of excavating a production line trench near the well head. At the time of inspection, I spoke with Range Resources representatives Nate Smiell and John Fountain I observed a thick black material approximately 2 feet below the well pad furnace adjacent ot the 5H well (API 37-125-28720). A drill rig was not located on site. Mr. Smiell indicated that drilling was completed at the end of October 2019 and the well was in the process of being equipped for production prior to the stimulation of the well. The interior of the 5H well cellar was stained black. According to Mr. Smiell the black staining was part OBM and part spray adhesive residue from the installation of secondary containment. Additionally, after drilling was complete the secondary containment was removed. Mr. Smiell indicated that no observation of OBM or staining was made until the report on 11/23/2019. The reviewed the PPC and ER plan. I requested that the Operator add the Gator Sorb that was being utilized as part of the clear up process to the SDS sheets on site. I also requested an electronic copy of the Gator Sorb SDS sheets. I reviewed the E&S plan associated with the site. The key way drains were marked on the E&S plan. A Department WQS (BAM) approved reline changes to the E&S plan on 5/23/2019 and 7/8/2019. The key way drains appeared to be approved via red line change on 7/8/2019. I inspected the key way drains and sediment trap #2. No observation of sheen or OBM was made at any of the key way drains or sediment trap #2. It appears that the released material is localized to the well pad. I reviewed the E&S well pad grading plan, it appears that the lowest spot on the well pad is the ear near the 5H well. I recommend that the Operator continue with the remediation process and to monitor the key way drains and waters of the commonwealth for evidence that the release spread WOC. I was unbale to positively identify the sources of the released material. Violations are being issued related to the release of material to the ground surface and additional violation maybe forth coming based on the Departments investigation.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/27/2025
Comments: On August 27, 2025, the Department met on-site with the Operator and Moody and Associates to assess the access road culvert inlet. Accompanying me today is Lisa Raffle (Diversified), Glenn Wilson (Diversified), Jessie Bobrzynski (Moody), and Jona Stoskey (Moody).Due to the approximate specific conductivity threshold of 4.00 mS (according to Moody and Associates), the stained area observed in IR 4040776 on the access road will not be assessed. During today's on-site inspection/meeting, specific conductivity of the soil under the rip rap of the access road's culvert inlet was measured by the Department and Moody. Moody utilized their own specific conductivity probe/meter as well as a probe/meter supplied by Diversified. The Department utilized its own specific conductivity probe/meter. All three specific conductivity probes/meters were calibrated on-site prior to the inspection/meeting.Upon arrival to the culvert inlet, Lisa Raffle of Diversified informed the Department that she took readings of specific conductivity following the Department's latest on-site inspection (IR 4040776), to which she did not observe readings anywhere near as high as the Department did. The Department asked Raffle where the readings were taken from, to which Raffle indicated it was from the excavated area (Photo 2) within the culvert ditch. This small excavated area is observed to be upslope of the culvert and just downslope of the access road. The Department clarified that each of the specific conductivity readings for this inlet that were probed by the Department in previous on-site inspection were probed directly in front of the culvert inlet.Specific conductivity readings were probed by Moody and the Department in front of, under, and on the sides of the culvert inlet. Readings were observed to be 'Or' (Out of Range) or above 20.0 mS underneath and to the right (South) of the culvert. Glenn Wilson (Diversified) promptly removed approximately one and a half 5-gallon buckets of impacted material from this area (Photo 3).Following the removal of this material, Moody probed again and recorded readings between 6.0-10.0 mS underneath the culvert inlet. At this time, Diversified and Moody jointly decided to halt removal of material and collect a soil sample of the soil that was producing the 6.0-10.0 mS readings. The Department also collected a soil sample (SAC 960) from this location following Moody's collection. Based on today's inspection, all issued violations remain outstanding.

Comments: On January 13, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of EQT's Herriott Well Pad after a spill was reported to the emergency hotline at 1:50pm on January 12, 2025. According to the spill report and a verbal conversation with Logan Dominick of EQT via the phone, at 1pm on 1/12/2025, a truck drove over a hose breaking the coupling on the hose releasing production fluids. Mr. Dominick stated that 90% of the spill occurred on containment and approximately 10% spilled off of containment. Mr. Dominick estimated that 10 gallons spilled and stated that SPSI scraped approximately 6 inches of the well pad in the spill area as well as vacuumed up the containment and placed all contaminated materials into a dumpster on site.At the time of this inspection EQT representative Jeremy Barber was on site and inform the Department that Flowback was currently occurring. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a section of the pad that was scrapped adjacent to two frack tanks that were in containment. The Department also observed a dumpster adjacent to the spill area. In the middle of the spill area appeared to be a strip of containment that had hoses in it. Mr. Barber pointed out that the open hose was the one that was ran over and caused the spill. The Department did not observe any holes or tears in the hose containment or the frack tank containment and the containments appeared to be dry.Background conductivity readings were taken adjacent to the well pad on the perimeter and some vegetation (0.289mS) and then readings were taken in the spill area that was scraped (0.0945 mS, 0.0386, 0.0416mS), then a reading was taken outside but directly adjacent to the spill area (0.0036 mS). Mr. Barber informed the Department that the area underneath these containments had not been scraped yet and that as soon as Flowback is completed, they will be pulled, the area beneath them will be scraped, and any contaminated material will be properly disposed of. The Department took conductivity readings at the edge/underneath this containment to determine if this area is contaminated, and the readings are as follows: 3.34 mS and 1.649 under/adjacent to the containment of the frack tanks where the spill occurred, and 13.98 mS under/adjacent to the containment where the hose is and where the spill originated. The soil conductivity readings in the spill area where the ground has been scraped, is comparable to the background reading and therefore appears to be remediated in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills, however, the readings in the area at the edge of/underneath the containment lining were elevated compared to the background reading and therefore appears to still be contaminated. The Department verbally recommended to Mr. Barber that the containment be lifted and materials be scraped as soon as possible. Mr. Barber informed The Department that SPSI will be back on site today and they will continue to remediate the release in accordance with policies. Mr. Barber also stated that photo documentation of continued remediate efforts will be supplied to the Department as soon as it is available. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection and the spill not being completely remediated yet, violations are being issued for an approximately 10 gallon release of production fluid from a hose onto the well pad.

Comments: The DEP completed an administrative inspection on Blackhill Energy's Kinglsey E 7H well(API 015-23676) located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 12/7/2021. The inspection was completed in order to summarize sample results from a sample collected during the 11/10/2021 inspection (IR #3282018). On 11/10/2021, I inspected Blackhill Energy's Kingsley E well site and discovered elevated electrical conductivity puddles off of the pad-wide containment. Elevated electrical conductivity puddles were field measured utilizing an Oakton PCSTestr 35 and ranged in field readings from 5.4 to 9.0 mS/cm. A sample for standard analysis code 942 was collected on 11/10/2021 from a puddle field measured at ~7.7mS/cm (0983-254). The sample was later received by the DEP Laboratory in Harrisburg, PA on 11/16/2021 and the final sample results were reported on 12/4/2021. The DEP's analytical sample results are attached as photos and as a file. Additional information regarding the initial inspection can be found in inspection record #3282018. The operator responded immediately after notification of the discovery. The operator believed the containment berms were driven over and crushed, which allowed the elevated electrical conductivity water that was on containment to be spilled off of containment. The operator estimated the back (northeastern) side to be less than 1 gallon while the front (southwestern) side was reported to be less than 4 gallons, but was then mixed with freshwater which was sprayed on the pad for dust control. The operator explained that they planned on remediating the impacted area and placing rig mats in front of the driving areas, so trucks will drive over the rig mats and not over the containment berms. At around 1500 hours the next day, 11/11/2021, the operator provided me photos of the remediation (see photos #3 & 4). Based on the findings of inspection record #3282018 and sample results 0983-254 violations of the following are cited against API # 015-23676: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 35 P.S. 6018.301 Due to the timely response of remediation efforts completed by the operator, these violations will be cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED and will be closed at this time.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/26/2024 to APOLLO RESOURCES LLC in Nicholson Township, Fayette county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: APOLLO RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/26/2024
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8209585
Permit API: 051-23812
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Nicholson Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/26/2024
Comments: On November 26, 2024, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a referral from OGI Charles Reaggle (IR 3864611 on 10/18/2024). OGI Charles Reaggle requested that a WQS follow up because of observed fluid dripping from both annulus wings. Well appears to be equipped for production. Site is well vegetated.Well tag requirement fulfilled with API number present on production tank. Well posting for Big Dog Energy does not appear to be correct Operator. In IR 3864611, the Department noted that the well transferred Operators from Big Dog Energy to Dorso LP, however the well has since transferred again to Apollo Resources as of October 30, 2024. The Department recommends Apollo Resources fulfill the well posting requirement in accordance with OGA3211(G).Drip still observed coming from the annulus. Specific conductivity was measured inside the annulus (7.62 mS / 7,620 uS), in the soil below the annulus (1.161 mS / 1,161 uS), and three background points of the soil surrounding the site (0.1805 mS / 180.5 uS), (0.1524 mS / 152.4 uS), (0.262 mS / 262 uS). These measurements of specific conductivity indicate that a release of brine has occurred from the annulus. The Department recommends the Operator repair the annulus to prevent further release. The Department recommends the Operator remove all impacted soil/material and properly disposing of the soil/material.Production tank on site and appears to be structurally sound at this time. Violations are being issued for release of production fluid to the ground. Previously issued violations in IR 3864611 by OGI Charles Reaggle are being evaluated under enforcement ID 435756.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.

Violation ID: 8268867
Permit API: 125-29232
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Nottingham Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/23/2026
Comments: On March 23, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the Sanns Frank well site. The inspection is separated into 3 inspection reports due to number of photos. This is inspection 1 of 3.The ESCGP (ESG076322011-00) for this site was issued on 8/27/2021 and was set to expire on 8/26/2026, but was terminated on 11/6/2024 (IRs 3862784 and 3863032).There are 8 total wells on-site at this time. The 1H, 2H, 3H, and 7H appear to be completed and equipped for production at this time. The 4H, 5H, 6H, and 8H appear to have recently completed drilling activities and are currently not in production.Act 9 sign is present and complies with 78a55 fabrication requirements. Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, and ESCGP plans are all present on site. The ERP and PPC plans include the required components.Wet Pond (Photos 4-5) appears to be functioning properly, no E and S issues observed at this time.The area below the outlet and level spreader of MRC Rain Garden #2 (Photos 8-17) appears to be heavily saturated with lack of vegetation and exposed earth as the water flows towards UNT to Mingo Creek. The water appears to be exiting the level spreader in sheet flow, but appears to be channelizing as it exits the LOD into the tree line. At this time, the water is entering the stream but no active sediment discharge is observed.The access road crossing of UNT to Mingo Creek (Photos 22-25) is observed with CFS installed on both sides of the access road. The CFS appears to have been installed properly but appears to have not been maintained and is failing, allowing mud to exit the access road via undercutting. The mud is observed to continuing down the slope below the access road into a pond of water on the East side, which also continues via channelized flow into UNT to Mingo Creek. What appears to be dust from the access road is also observed on the surface below the access road on the East side and is observed on most of the leaf cover in this area. At this time, no active sediment discharge is observed into the stream.On the West side, it appears that the extent of the dust and mud ends within the rip rap, however some gravel is observed off the access road.The rock apron below Channel 8 and the level spreader below MRC Rain Garden #3 both appear to be discharging stormwater in sheet flow, however the vegetation below both features is heavily saturated and the stormwater appears to be channelizing closer to the tree line, where it eventually reaches UNT to Mingo Creek. This area also appears to be impacted by a two track trail. At this time, no active sediment discharge is observed into the stream.Additional vegetation disturbances are observed along the access road (Photos 7-9, 13). No E and S issues are observed in these areas at this time. The DEP recommends the operator stabilize these areas.A small release of what appears to be a petroleum-based fluid is observed on the access road near the mailbox (Photos 18-19). The DEP spoke to Scott Clark (Range Resources) during discovery of the release. Clark appeared to be leaving the well pad and informed the DEP that he was unaware of the release, but would have personnel clean it up today.The DEP recommends the operator properly dispose of the impacted material and requests the disposal documents when made available. No violation is being issued for the release at this time due to the volume of the release appearing to be below reporting limits.Well equipment on the well pad appears to be contained within secondary containment and no other spills, leaks, or releases were observed on the well pad at this time.Wooden stakes with ribbons attached are observed at several disturbed areas on-site and near UNT to Mingo. The DEP requests additional information in regard to the stakes.Violations for accelerated erosion and sedimentation, failed E and S BMPs, and failure to maintain PCSM BMP are being issued at this time.
